note: First objective-practice batch. Descriptive answer banks, RTC, essay and letter model-answer items will be added in subsequent batches.

questions.question: What did Lencho hope for when he looked towards the sky?
questions.explanation: Lencho needed rain for his crop and hoped that the rain would come.

questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: Where did Nelson Mandela's inauguration take place?
questions.explanation: Mandela's inauguration took place at the Union Buildings in Pretoria.

questions.question: Why was the young seagull afraid to fly?
options: He thought his wings would not support him
questions.explanation: He feared that his wings would not support him in the air.

questions.question: What did the pilot see when he looked at the sky ahead?
questions.explanation: He saw huge black clouds ahead and entered the storm.

questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: What name did Anne Frank give to her diary?
questions.explanation: Anne addressed her diary as Kitty.

questions.question: What traditional occupation is central to A Baker from Goa?
questions.explanation: The chapter recalls Goa's traditional bread-making culture.

questions.question: What did Pranjol and Rajvir travel to Assam to see?
questions.explanation: They travelled to Assam and saw extensive tea plantations.

questions.question: What animal was Mijbil?
questions.explanation: Mijbil was an otter adopted by the narrator.

questions.question: What truth about life does Kisa Gotami learn?
questions.explanation: She learns that death is universal and no household is free from it.

questions.question: Why does Lomov visit Chubukov's house?
questions.explanation: Lomov comes to ask Natalya to marry him.

questions.question: What falls on the poet in Dust of Snow?
questions.explanation: A crow shakes dust of snow from a hemlock tree onto the poet.

questions.question: In Fire and Ice, what does fire symbolise?
questions.explanation: Fire represents desire or uncontrolled passion.

questions.question: Where is the tiger confined?
questions.explanation: The tiger is kept in a concrete cell in the zoo.

questions.question: Which animal is described as having a hide that is yellow and black?
questions.explanation: The poem humorously describes the Bengal Tiger by its yellow-and-black appearance.

questions.question: What does the boy learn through losing his ball?
options: How to buy a new ball
questions.explanation: The loss becomes a lesson in accepting loss and responsibility.

questions.question: What do the trees symbolically want to do?
questions.explanation: The trees are personified as struggling to move out towards the forest.

questions.question: The fog is compared to which animal?
questions.explanation: The poet compares the fog to a cat that comes and leaves quietly.

questions.question: What may men love in Anne Gregory according to the speaker?
questions.explanation: The poem questions whether human love is attracted by physical beauty.

questions.question: What name did the narrator use when he met Anil?
questions.explanation: The narrator tells the story using the name Hari Singh.

questions.question: What did Matilda borrow from Mme Forestier?
questions.explanation: Matilda borrowed a necklace for the minister's ball.

questions.question: Why did Lencho compare the raindrops to new coins?
options: He believed the rain would bring a good harvest
He wanted to buy a house
He was collecting coins from the field
questions.explanation: Lencho depended on the rain for his crop, so rain meant prosperity to him.

questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: What does Mandela suggest about the oppressor?
options: Hatred and domination also damage the oppressor's humanity
questions.explanation: Mandela argues that a system of domination dehumanises the person who practises it as well as the victim.

questions.question: Why did the young seagull finally dive for the food?
options: Hunger overcame his fear and his mother tempted him with food
He had already learnt to fly
questions.explanation: His mother held food just out of reach, and hunger made him leap forward.

questions.question: Why is the ending of The Black Aeroplane mysterious?
options: The control tower says no other plane was in the sky
The pilot lands in another country
questions.explanation: The mystery comes from the strange plane being absent from the control tower's radar information.

questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: Why did Anne decide to write a diary?
options: She wanted a true friend with whom she could share her thoughts
She wanted to publish a novel immediately
Her teacher ordered her to do so
She wanted to record only school marks
questions.explanation: Anne treated her diary as a trusted friend because she felt paper had more patience than people.

questions.question: Why were bakers important in traditional Goan life?
options: Bread and bakery products were part of daily life and celebrations
questions.explanation: The chapter shows bread and the baker as important parts of Goan customs and celebrations.

questions.question: What made Mijbil especially interesting to the narrator?
options: His playful, curious and intelligent behaviour
questions.explanation: Mijbil is portrayed as curious, playful and inventive.

questions.question: How does Buddha help Kisa Gotami overcome her grief?
options: He asks her to find mustard seeds from a house untouched by death
He tells her to forget her son immediately
questions.explanation: The search makes her discover that every family has experienced death.

questions.question: What makes The Proposal comic?
options: A marriage proposal repeatedly turns into quarrels over trivial matters
questions.explanation: The characters argue over land and a dog even while discussing marriage.

questions.question: What was the main cause of Tricki's poor health?
questions.explanation: Mrs Pumphrey overfed Tricki and gave him too little exercise.

questions.question: Which statement best explains Rajvir's interest in tea?
options: He had read about tea and wanted to observe its history and cultivation closely
He wanted to stop tea production
He had never heard of tea
He wanted to become a railway officer
questions.explanation: Rajvir has read about tea and is fascinated by its origin, legends and cultivation.

questions.chapter: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom
questions.question: What two obligations does Mandela discuss?
options: Obligation to family and obligation to community or country
questions.explanation: Mandela explains that personal responsibilities and social demands can conflict under an unjust system.

questions.question: What lesson about overcoming fear is central to His First Flight?
options: Courage grows when one takes the first necessary step
questions.explanation: The young seagull discovers his ability only after taking the risk of flying.

questions.question: Why does the narrator feel grateful to the mysterious pilot?
options: The black aeroplane guides him safely through the storm
questions.explanation: The mysterious plane signals him to follow and leads him out of the storm.

questions.chapter: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.question: What does Anne's treatment of her teachers reveal about her personality?
options: She is observant, outspoken and capable of humour even when criticised
She is completely uninterested in school
She never thinks about her behaviour
questions.explanation: Anne reflects on her teachers and herself with honesty, wit and self-awareness.

questions.question: What change occurs in the poet's mood in Dust of Snow?
options: A gloomy mood changes into a more positive one
questions.explanation: The simple natural incident refreshes the poet and changes his mood.

questions.question: Why will another ball not really replace the lost one?
options: The boy's experience of loss and responsibility cannot be bought again
The new ball would be smaller
questions.explanation: The important loss is emotional and educational, not merely the loss of an object.

questions.question: What is the central symbolic idea of The Trees?
options: A longing for freedom and return to the natural world
questions.explanation: The personified trees symbolise a desire to escape confinement and return to nature.

questions.question: What major irony drives The Necklace?
options: Matilda suffers for years to replace a necklace that turns out to have been imitation
She becomes wealthy after losing it
questions.explanation: The final revelation shows that the original necklace was not valuable, making Matilda's hardship tragically ironic.

questions.question: How does education transform Bholi?
options: It gives her confidence and the ability to resist an unfair marriage
It makes her dislike her parents
questions.explanation: Education and her teacher's support help Bholi develop confidence, self-respect and independence.

questions.question: Which interpretation best captures the poem's warning?
options: Both uncontrolled desire and hatred can destroy the world
Nature alone is responsible for human conflict
questions.explanation: Fire symbolises desire and ice symbolises hatred; either can be destructive.

questions.question: Which contrast is most important in A Tiger in the Zoo?
options: The tiger's natural freedom is contrasted with his confinement in the cage
The tiger is contrasted with a dog only
Day is contrasted with night only
The zoo is contrasted with a market
questions.explanation: The poem contrasts the tiger's natural power and freedom with captivity.

questions.question: What does the chapter mainly preserve?
options: Memories of traditional Goan bread-making culture and its influence
A guide to farming in Goa
A story about a school examination
questions.explanation: The narrator recalls the baker, bread and bread-related customs in Goa.

questions.question: What is the deeper idea in For Anne Gregory?
options: Human beings may judge beauty externally, while divine love sees the inner self
Physical beauty has no effect on anyone
questions.explanation: The poem contrasts human attraction to outward beauty with the idea of divine love for the inner self.

questions.question: Which combination best explains Matilda's tragedy?
options: Dissatisfaction, vanity and the desire for social status lead to unnecessary suffering
Kindness and honesty make her poor
Her friends force her to attend the ball
questions.explanation: Matilda's dissatisfaction with her modest life and obsession with appearance lead to years of hardship.

questions.question: Choose the correct reported form: Riya said, "I am preparing for the examination."
options: Riya said that she was preparing for the examination.
Riya said that I am preparing for the examination.
Riya says that she was preparing for the examination.
Riya said that she is preparing for the examination yesterday.
questions.explanation: With a past reporting verb, present continuous commonly changes to past continuous and I changes to she.

questions.question: For a five-mark school essay, which plan is most effective?
options: Introduction, relevant organised points, examples where useful, and a clear conclusion
One very long sentence with no paragraphs
A paragraph unrelated to the topic
questions.explanation: A strong essay needs a clear structure, relevant development and an appropriate conclusion.
